gap: No result ChatGPT got states how fast an iPhone 17 actually charges wirelessly when someone outside Apple times it: CNET measured 49% in 30 minutes from a start of 10% or less, Macworld timed Apple's MagSafe puck at about 1 h 15 min to 80% and 2 h 06 min to full, and mac4ever measured a UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 25W charger at 38% in 30 minutes.
standout_why: The pages ChatGPT cited are Apple's iPhone 17 specs page and several copies of the Apple MagSafe Charger (1 m) store page. The specs page gives only Apple's own claim: 'Up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with 30W adapter or higher paired with MagSafe Charger', from tests Apple ran in July 2025 on preproduction phones. The MagSafe Charger page now cites tests on the 'iPhone Duo', does not mention the iPhone 17 and shows no price. The Bechtle results are copies of Apple's spec sheet. None of these pages has a measurement by an independent reviewer or lab, and none compares Apple's puck with a third-party Qi2/Qi2.2 charger on an iPhone 17.
decides: The independent tests back Apple's claim for its own MagSafe setup. CNET got 49% in 30 minutes on the iPhone 17, against Apple's claimed 50%. The only independent timing of a third-party Qi2 25W charger on an iPhone 17 (mac4ever, UGREEN MagFlow) came in lower, at 38% in 30 minutes and 35–40 minutes to 50%. That is slower than UGREEN's own claim of about 26 minutes. The two labs used different methods, and CNET did not name its charger in the coverage I could open. So the evidence leans toward Apple's MagSafe Charger with a 30W+ adapter as the safe pick for a measured 25W-class result. The page should label third-party '50% in 25 minutes' figures as the maker's claim, not a measurement.

findings.label: CNET 30-minute wireless charge test, battery gained
findings.value: iPhone 17: 49%; iPhone 17 Pro: 55%; iPhone 17 Pro Max: 53%; iPhone Air: 47%
findings.source_title: iPhone 17 Pro has the fastest charging speed of 33 phones tested (9to5Mac, Ben Lovejoy, 2026-05-14, reporting CNET's lab test)
findings.note: CNET lab test from May 2026, covering 33 phones. Each phone was drained to 10% or less, then charged for 30 minutes. Cult of Mac (David Snow, 2026-05-14, https://www.cultofmac.com/news/iphone-17-pro-wins-charging-speed-test) reports the same figures. CNET's original page (cnet.com/tech/mobile/cnet-lab-exclusive-fastest-wired-wireless-charging-phone/) could not be fetched, so these figures come from the coverage. Neither article names the wireless charger or adapter CNET used. Apple claims 50% in 30 min, so CNET's 49% roughly matches it, although CNET started from up to 10% rather than empty.

findings.label: Macworld timed wireless charge of an iPhone 17 on Apple's MagSafe puck
findings.value: 0–80% in about 1 h 15 min; 0–100% in 2 h 06 min (iPhone 17e with 15 W MagSafe: about 2 h 15 min and 3 h 03 min)
findings.source_title: The iPhone 17e proves MagSafe charging speeds don't matter (Macworld, David Price, 2026-03-19)
findings.note: Both phones were fully drained, then charged on an official Apple MagSafe charging puck powered by a 67 W adapter. The article does not report a 0–50% time.

findings.label: Peak wireless power into a standard iPhone 17 (ChargerLAB)
findings.source_title: Regular iPhone 17's USB-C Charging Speeds Tested With Apple Chargers (MacRumors, Joe Rossignol, 2025-09-26)
findings.note: MacRumors attributes this figure to ChargerLAB. It is a peak, not a sustained rate, and Apple rates sustained MagSafe charging at 25 W. The adapter is not named. ChargerLAB's own iPhone 17 compatibility page (https://www.chargerlab.com/charging-compatibility-test-of-iphone-17/, Joey, 2025-09-26) shows only wired results, so I could not open the primary source for this number.

findings.label: mac4ever timed charge over Qi2 25W, battery after 30 minutes
findings.value: iPhone 17: 38%; iPhone 17 Pro: 45%; iPhone 17 Pro Max: 39%; iPhone Air: 36%; 35–40 min to reach 50%
findings.source_title: Test des chargeurs UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 25W, idéals pour l'iPhone 17 (mac4ever, Didier Pulicani, 2025-10-18)
findings.note: The article tested three UGREEN MagFlow products (10,000 mAh power bank, 2-in-1 and 3-in-1, all 25 W). It does not say which product was used for each phone, and it reports no temperatures. Compared with CNET's iPhone 17 result: 38% vs 49% in 30 min, 11 points lower. The labs used different methods and start levels, so read this as an indication only. UGREEN claims about 26 min to 50% for an iPhone 17 Pro Max.

findings.label: 9to5Mac reviewer's observed charge in 30 minutes
findings.source_title: ESR delivers near-wired charging speeds with its new Qi 2.2 3-in-1 charging station (9to5Mac, Bradley Chambers, 2025-12-15)
findings.note: This is the reviewer's own observation, not a logged lab test, and the iPhone model is not named (iPhone 16 or 17 on iOS 26 required). The station comes with a 50 W adapter. Chambers says he could not measure temperatures himself. ESR claims an average of 6.5° cooler.

unsourced: Which wireless charger and adapter CNET used for its iPhone tests: cnet.com would not load, and the 9to5Mac and Cult of Mac summaries leave it out.

AppleInsider's measured times for the Anker Prime Wireless Charging Station 3-in-1 on an iPhone 17 Pro: the review URL returned HTTP 403 twice (regular and AMP URLs), so the search-snippet figure of about 27 min to 50% is left out.

Any independent timed or thermal measurement of the Belkin UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1 (WIZ040) on an iPhone 17: searched for reviews; found only Belkin's claims, retailer reviews and Pickr/WhistleOut write-ups with no numbers.

Independent measurements of the ESR Cyclone 25W pad and of the UGREEN MagFlow Qi2.2 25W pad by name on an iPhone 17: none found. techtest.org's review of the UGREEN W711 (Michael Barton, 2025-10-10) measured only 1.24 W idle draw, with no charge curve.
A reviewer's temperature measurements (°F/°C) of fan-cooled and fanless 25 W chargers on an iPhone 17: every cooling figure I found is a maker claim (ESR, Belkin, Anker).
Galaxus's Qi2 comparison test (galaxus.de page 40668): the page timed out on both attempts.
ChargerLAB's primary article for the 29 W MagSafe peak on the iPhone 17: chargerlab.com's iPhone 17 page holds only wired results.
